pressure.title: Two correction planes cancel static and couple unbalance
pressure.description: An unbalanced rotor's heavy spot creates a rotating centrifugal force F = m·e·ω², which shakes the soft pedestals at once per revolution. The pick-ups measure amplitude; the photo-cell gives the phase, so the console calculates the correction mass and angle for each of two planes (dynamic unbalance = static + couple). Residual unbalance is checked against the required grade, e.g. ISO 21940-11 G6.3 for fans and pump impellers or G2.5 for turbine rotors: U_per = G·m / ω (g·mm).

video_tutorials.title: Dynamic Balancing Machine — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Dynamic Balancing Machine.

A dynamic balancing machine spins a rotor on sensitive pedestals, measures the once-per-revolution vibration caused by unbalance and its phase (from a reference mark), and computes the mass and angle of correction in two planes so both static and couple unbalance are removed to the required grade.
Typical applications include fan rotors, pump impellers, motor rotors after repair; turbine and compressor rotors, rolls and crankshafts.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Fan Rotor on Arbor: Heavy Spot (red) & Correction Weight (green), Reflective Reference Mark, Universal-Joint Drive Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Dynamic Balancing Machine.
Check rollers and sensors.
Verify with test rotor.
Calibration per ISO 21940-21.
Watch for non-repeatable results: readings vary. Common cause: loose parts on rotor, worn rollers.
Watch for wrong angle: correction worsens. Common cause: reference mark / sensor misread.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
